Approved September 16, 2026

# Derry Planning Board Minutes of September 02, 2026

The Planning Board for the Town of Derry held a public meeting on Wednesday, September 02, 2026, at 7:00 p.m. The meeting was broadcast from the Derry Municipal Center, 14 Manning Street, Third Floor meeting room, with a virtual option.

Members present: Dave Nelson, Chair, John O'Connor, Vice Chair, Richard Malaby, Secretary, Randy Chase, Town Council Liaison, Brian Chirichiello, Town Administrator Representative, Derek Minervini, Bryan Fishman, and Jacob Pelletier, Members, and Thomas Mauzy, Z. Michael Appleton, and Andrew Young, Alternates

Members absent: Michael Wood

Also present: Elizabeth Robidoux, Planning Director, Mark L'Heureux, Deputy Director of Public Works, Sam Fazioli, Engineering Coordinator, Beverly Donovan, Economic Development Director, Caroline Wilson, Planning Administrative Secretary II

Mr. Nelson opened the meeting at 7:00 p.m. The meeting began with a salute to the flag.

Mr. Young was seated for Mr. Wood.

## Escrow

**#26-31**

**Project Name: Birch Street Subdivision**

**Developer: 71 Birch Street, LLC**

**Escrow Account: Same**

**Escrow Type: Letter of Credit**

**Parcel ID/Location: 28001 and 28002, 4 Eden & 71 Birch Street**

The request is to approve a release of Letter of Credit # 82410756, drawn on Haverhill Bank, in the amount of $38,939.00, for the above noted project and request a replacement Letter of Credit or other form of security in the amount of $1,972.25.

> Motion by O'Connor, seconded by Malaby, to approve Escrow #26-31 as presented.
>
> Roll Call Vote: Chase, Young, Minervini, O'Connor, Fishman, Pelletier, Chirichiello, Malaby, and Nelson vote Yes. The motion passed.

**#26-32**

**Project Name: 75.5 Fordway Extension Subdivision**

**Developer: Dreamcatcher Homes, LLC**

**Escrow Account: Same**

**Escrow Type: Letter of Credit**

**Parcel ID/Location: 21009, 75.5 Fordway Extension**

The request is to approve a release of Letter of Credit # 82468234, drawn on Haverhill Bank, in the amount of $24,719.25, for the above noted project and request a replacement Letter of Credit or other form of security in the amount of $1,150.00.

> Motion by O'Connor, seconded by Malaby, to approve Escrow #26-32 as presented.
>
> Roll Call Vote: Chase, Young, Minervini, O'Connor, Fishman, Pelletier, Chirichiello, Malaby, and Nelson vote Yes. The motion passed.

## Minutes

The Board reviewed the minutes of the August 05, 2026 public meeting.

> Motion by O'Connor, seconded by Malaby, to approve the minutes of the August 05, 2026 public meeting as written.
>
> Roll Call Vote: Young, Minervini, O'Connor, Fishman, Chirichiello, Malaby, and Nelson vote Yes. Chase and Pelletier abstained due to being absent. The motion passed.

## Correspondence

Mr. Malaby reported that the September / October edition of *Town and City Magazine* is now available.

## Other Business

### Second Extension Request

**PID 05062, 05063, 05064, 05065-001**

**1, 2, 3, and 4 Humphrey Road**

**Timothy J. Butterfield June 1997 Rev. Trust,**

**Sharon L. Butterfield June 1997 Rev. Trust,**

**Humphrey Road, LLC**

Ms. Robidoux explained the Planning Board approved a mixed use site plan for the Butterfield Revocable Trusts, and Humphrey Road, LLC on September 18, 2024. The Board also granted a request to extend the deadline to meet the conditions of approval to September 18, 2026. The applicant has secured required State approvals related to the realignment of Humphrey Road where it intersects with North Main Street. The applicant is requesting a second extension for an additional 12 months to finalize the remaining conditions precedent which include the following:

1. Owner's signature (obtained)
2. Establish construction escrow for the project and unset bounds
3. GIS Disk submission
4. Submission of Fair Share contribution for future signal improvements at Webster's Corner
5. Submission of final plan sets for signature (*received by the Planning Department*)

Staff recommends the Board grant up to a 12 month extension of the approval. The new expiration date would then be September 18, 2027.

Mr. Chase added that last night, the Town Council accepted the drainage easements for the realignment of Humphrey Road.

> Motion by O'Connor, seconded by Malaby to grant a 12 month extension of the approval for the mixed use development at PID 05062, 05063, 05064, and 05065-001; 1, 2, 3, and 4 Humphrey Road. The new expiration date will be September 18, 2027.
>
> Roll Call Vote: Chase, Young, Minervini, O'Connor, Fishman, Pelletier, Chirichiello, Malaby, and Nelson vote Yes. The motion passed.

### Façade Improvements

**PID 35014-005, 20 Folsom Road**

**Royal T Car Wash**

Ms. Robidoux explained the Messinas have asked the Board to review a change to the color of the siding of the business to dark gray as well as the addition of an architectural element to the bottom of the building. Renderings have been provided to the Board.

The Town of Derry Planning Board has the authority, per the Land Development Control Regulations, Section 170-83.A, to review changes that would affect the exterior of a building. Specifically in Section 170-84.A.3, alterations to structures within the Industrial II zoning district shall have a Medium High level of compliance with the regulations. Section 170-86.F.8 speaks to the color of a building, and specifically states 'subtle colors are appropriate on larger, plainer buildings, whereas smaller buildings with more detailing can more effectively incorporate brighter colors. Bright colors should be limited to accent areas. High intensity colors, metallic colors, or fluorescent colors should not be used'.

Staff recommends the Board review this change to the exterior of the building and to make a finding of fact.

> Motion by O'Connor, seconded by Malaby, that after review of the proposal, the Board finds the proposed façade renovation of Royal T Carwash, PID 35014-005, 20 Folsom Road is appropriate for the Industrial II Zoning District as:
>
> The proposed change demonstrates overall compliance with the Architectural Design Regulations
>
> The proposed change does not detrimentally affect the nature of the surrounding uses, the style of the surrounding buildings, or special feature of historic, cultural or community interest in the vicinity of the project.
>
> The proposed color (Dark Gray), and the addition of faux granite along the bottom of the façade is appropriate for the neighborhood and the district.
>
> Roll Call Vote: Chase, Young, Minervini, O'Connor, Fishman, Pelletier, Chirichiello, Malaby, and Nelson vote Yes. The motion passed.

### Architectural Design Review - Sign in TBOD

**PID 30051, 16 Manning Street, Unit 101**

**On the Road to Wellness**

Ms. Robidoux explained the Town of Derry Zoning Ordinance, Section 165-101.5 (A)(1)(q), requires that all new signs proposed in the Traditional Business Overlay District be reviewed by the Planning Board prior to the issuance of a sign permit. The Board is familiar with the sign requirements in the TBOD.

The applicant is proposing signage as noted on the attached exhibit. The identification sign is 3.3 SF and the sign above the unit is 14.25 SF. Per the ordinance, applicants are permitted to have 1 sf of sign per 1 ft of road frontage, with a minimum of 20 SF permitted; aggregate total of all signs for the business cannot exceed 50 SF. This request meets the zoning requirements for signs in the TBOD.

On the Road to Wellness is currently operating at 16 Manning Street, Unit 101.

Staff recommends the Board approve the proposed signage.

> Motion by O'Connor, seconded by Malaby, pursuant to the Town of Derry Zoning Ordinance, Article XII, Signs, Section 165-101.5, Signs in the TBOD, to approve the sign design presented for On the Road to Wellness, Parcel 30051, 16 Manning Street, Unit 101, as presented. The Board finds the sign is compatible with the surrounding buildings, meets the regulations contained in the Ordinance, and compliments the surrounding architecture.
>
> Roll Call Vote: Chase, Young, Minervini, O'Connor, Fishman, Pelletier, Chirichiello, Malaby, and Nelson vote Yes. The motion passed.

### Planning Director and Chairman Updates

Ms. Robidoux announced that the changes to the Zoning Ordinance and the LDCR relative to the Central Business District (CBD) will be effective tomorrow. Please email Ms. Wilson if you would like a hard copy of either document.

No plans were submitted for the September 16th meeting. Ms. Robidoux offered to bring draft changes to the Zoning Ordinance related to the 2026 legislative changes to the Board for administrative review that evening; Mr. Nelson agreed with utilizing meeting time for review.

The Plans Reading and Analysis workshop will be in the Municipal Center Meeting Room, 8:30-noon, on September 25th. Interested Board members should email Ms. Wilson to register.

The GovWell permitting platform officially went live today; all Planning Board, Planning Department, and ZBA applications will be submitted through this system. Applicants will still be required to submit paper plan sets. The application review format will remain unchanged for the Boards. Health, Service Requests (Code), Building, and Fire Prevention permits will be phased in and by the end of the calendar year should be accessible via GovWell.

Mr. Nelson urged all to vote in the Primary election on September 08.

## Public Hearing

### Bird Enterprises, LLC

**PID 10012, 187 Hampstead Road**

**Acceptance/Review**

**Site Plan Amendment - Addition of Nursery Stock Area**

Ms. Robidoux explained Bird Enterprises purchased the property located at 187 Hampstead Road which was the former Holy Cross Church. Delahunty Garden and Landscape Center relocated from Windham to this location and the former church has been renovated to create an indoor youth sports training facility known as Northeast Elite Athletics. The property is located in the LMDR zone. Water service is supplied by the Pennichuck system. The Planning Board approved the site plan in 2025. On that plan, the Board approved material storage and pick up areas, stock areas, parking for company vehicles/equipment storage and associated parking. The applicant has expanded uses on the lot. Changes from the approved plan include:

1. Retail display areas outside the main building entrance have been discontinued.
2. A 10 x 20' storage container has been added behind the building.
3. 133 arbor vitae have been added along the perimeter of the north, east and south sides of the property to address staff concerns that the residential buffer had been removed.
4. There has been an addition of stock area on either side of the training facility and in landscaped islands to the left of the main entrance.
5. The equipment storage area is now a nursery stock area.
6. A shed, greenhouse, and a 10 x 20' storage container have been added near the rear of the lot.
7. The 'check in' shed has been removed and a dumpster added.
8. It appears the tree line on the right hand side of the property adjacent to the wetlands has been removed.

There was concern that stock was being placed in wetland buffers and treatment swales. During the August 29, 2025, TRC meeting it was stated: "The wetlands were flagged when the property was first developed as a church in 1999. Recently, Delahunty Nursery and Northeast Elite Athletics moved onto the site, and Mr. Yennaco had the wetlands re-delineated by Thomas Sokoloski, CWS. It appears that about half of the area deemed to be wetlands in 1999 is no longer considered to be wetlands. Therefore, the proposed site plan amendment is for a 14' footpath to allow access to the uplands for storage of nursery stock (trees, shrubs.) The storage area is wooded, and will remain so, to conserve water. Nursery stock would be moved by hand or by a skid steer (with a track that is less than 4.7 PSF, which is lighter than a standard lawnmower.)" That 14 foot path is now a 9 foot wide, mulched path.

The existing sign location is shown on Sheet 2. As this project is located in a residential district, the ZBA has jurisdiction over the size of the sign.

The Police Department had a concern that the stock area to the front of the parcel could interfere with sight distance for those exiting the property. Stock should be situated so that it is set far enough back to not impede sight distance.

The nursery use is agricultural in nature under the definitions in the State statute. Photos provided by the applicant have been included in the Board's packets. Two letters of support were provided by the applicant today and were added to the Board's packets.

There are no waiver requests.

Staff recommends the Board to discuss the proposed changes to the site, and if the Board wishes, make a determination with regard to regional impact.

The applicant, Jay Yennaco, and his attorney, Chris Drescher, appeared before the Board.

> Motion by O'Connor, seconded by Malaby, to accept jurisdiction of the amended site plan application before the Board for Bird Enterprises, PID 10012, 187 Hampstead Road.
>
> Roll Call Vote: Chase, Young, Minervini, O'Connor, Fishman, Pelletier, Chirichiello, Malaby, and Nelson vote Yes. The motion passed.

> Motion by O'Connor, seconded by Malaby, pursuant to RSA 36:56, the Board finds the proposal as presented at this time meets the definition of a development of regional impact.
>
> Roll Call Vote: Chase, Young, Minervini, O'Connor, Fishman, Pelletier, Chirichiello, Malaby, and Nelson vote No, this is a minor site plan amendment and does not meet the definition of a development of regional impact.

> Motion by Chirichiello, seconded by Malaby, to open the Public Hearing.
>
> All members present vote Yes. The motion passed.

Mr. Yennaco introduced himself to the Board and provided the following information:

Mr. Yennaco is the owner of Bird Enterprises and both businesses in the building. Mr. Yennaco came before the Board roughly a year ago to talk about similar items to today. Since that time, they have moved in and established themselves, and those that drive by can see that they have cleaned up the property and begun to conduct business at both the nursery and indoor sports facility. Minor adjustments have been made since that time. Mr. Yennaco and Attorney Drescher of Cronin, Bisson, and Zalinsky are here to go over those adjustments with the Board.

Some items that were originally approved were taken away; such as a shed out front, which is no longer there. They are approved to have nursery stock by the road. (During the initial TRC review) the Police Department requested that line of sight should not be obstructed; the nursery has not put anything by the road to keep the line of sight clear and to allow passersby to see the building from the road. A couple of storage units and a dumpster were added. The dumpster is hidden behind the building and is not visible. On the plan, it says the shed is being replaced by a dumpster. The shed is being replaced on the property by a dumpster but it is not visible from the road. The sheds are either hidden behind the building or are at the back of the property out of sight from the road.

The primary concern today is the proposed tree and shrub storage area. Mr. Yennaco has had the wetlands re-delineated (they were last delineated in 1999). It was stated that this became a drier area; however, the area Mr. Yennaco is asking to use was always dry. There is a small path used to cross about 14' – 16' of wet area to reach the proposed storage area. The stream flows around the backside of the proposed storage area in the spring.

Mr. Yennaco recalled that a year ago, there were questions about fertilizer use. Nothing has changed on those specifications. Mr. Yennaco is only asking to increase the footprint of the storage area. There will be no structures placed in that area. There are no roadways, power, or utilities in that area.

Mr. Yennaco noted that the original approved plan called for 28 arbor vitae to be planted in the front of the property to screen the bulk storage area. Mr. Yennaco purchased 130 arbor vitae and has planted them in the front as well as around the sides of the property to proactively buffer the neighbors on either side. Underbrush and saplings were cut back and dead trees were removed. No vegetation was removed in the wetland.

Two letters of support were provided to the Planning Department today by Mr. Yennaco. These two abutters occupy the lots on either side of the parcel.

Mr. Nelson asked that both of the letters be transcribed into the minutes; no members of the Board objected.

### Email from Kate Lamb (2 Village Brook Lane) to Jay Yennaco, dated 09/01/2026:

They have been a huge improvement, and I feel much safer with them as neighbors. I fully support them expanding their nursery storage area. The business is always well kept and a pleasant sight to drive by. Delahunty's has been a welcoming addition to the vacant church and our neighborhood.

Mr. Nelson opened the floor to the Board.

Mr. Chirichiello asked for clarification on whether the proposed tree and shrub storage area was previously considered wetland. Mr. Yennaco said no, the proposed area is an upland and always has been an upland. It is flat but raised. Mr. Chirichiello inquired if this parcel was in the 100-year or 500-year floodplain; Ms. Robidoux said to the best of her knowledge it is not, there is just a lot of wetland.

Mr. Chirichiello asked if the plants are plants to be sold; Mr. Yennaco said yes, they are balled and burlapped or planted in containers.

Mr. Mauzy asked if the area in blue around the proposed tree and shrub storage area was wetland, and whether there would be an increase in foot traffic or in utility vehicle traffic. Mr. Yennaco said yes, it is wetland, but no, there will not be an increase in foot or vehicle traffic. Mr. Yennaco explained that the design specifically allows for the area to be accessed on high and dry land, either via foot or small machine.

Mr. Nelson opened to the floor to members of the Public, in-person or online.

### Tom Cardon, 2 Cunningham Drive

Mr. Cardon noticed wetlands on the GIS. Mr. Cardon lives about a mile down the road. Mr. Cardon used to have a large area of his own lawn that he could not mow until August or September. However, that area has not been wet for the last couple of years, and Mr. Cardon believes the water level has gone down. He was concerned about the location of the proposed shrub and tree area, were those wet areas?

Mr. Yennaco stated that he has had the wetlands redelineated.

Mr. Cardon inquired if that was something the Conservation Commission needed to look at.

Mr. Nelson added that the way that wetlands are delineated is by examining the soils and the types of plants that are present. Water may dry up in a season, but the plants and soils don't change.

Mr. Yennaco stated that his wetland scientist examined plants that are in the ground, plants that have died off, and also took core samples of soil 12" – 18" deep.

Mr. Cardon inquired about the water service. Was it Pennichuck, or Town water? Mr. Cardon explained that the 105 houses in his neighborhood are served by 2 Pennichuck wells. Five years ago, each well had 34 GPM, so 68 GPM total. Now it is down to 34 GPM. Mr. Cardon is concerned about water usage generated by the addition of the tree and shrub storage.

Mr. Chase stated that the subject property was fed from the Town of Derry water system, when it was extended up Hampstead Road. It is tied into the Manchester Water Works via the Derry water system. Mr. Fazioli confirmed this was correct. The Pennichuck system Mr. Cardon referred to is a separate system, not fed by Manchester Water Works.

Mr. Cardon inquired how many trees and shrubs would be stored there at any given time. Mr. Yennaco said a couple hundred.

### Andrew Rojee, 164 Hampstead Road

Mr. Rojee stated that it appears that the new area is actually an island surrounded by wetlands. Mr. Rojee understood that Mr. Yennaco previously stated that they don't use fertilizers.

Mr. Yennaco stated that was correct.

Mr. Rojee inquired if any of Mr. Yennaco's suppliers used fertilizers. How do we know whether the shrubs have fertilizers in them, and if it is running into the wetland?

Mr. Yennaco stated that when he presented to the Board last year, he detailed the process of what growers are regulated to do per the USDA. They are not allowed to ship balled and burlapped trees that have been fertilized within a certain amount of time. So, when the plants arrive at nurseries, and then are replanted in customers' yards, they are free of fertilizers. Mr. Yennaco receives certifications with every load of stock he receives certifying this. Container plants come with slow release pellets in them. Those pellets are designed to only release when the temperature of the soil is between 75-80° F, for a period of 20 to 30 days or longer. Plants are classified by zones, and the fertilizers activate in zone 6 or greater. This region is zone 4 to 5. Delahunty's does not have the certifications to fertilize or feed plants. The property is walked 3-5 times per year by the NH Department of Agriculture, which monitors concerns like invasive insects and unapproved practices. If the Department of Agriculture saw fertilizers on plants which Delahunty's was not certified to use, they would not be in business long.

Mr. Rojee still questions having over 100 plants in a concentrated area surrounded by wetlands. Mr. Rojee felt that some kind of environmental survey should be done to ensure there won't be impact.

Mr. Yennaco noted that lawn fertilizers that consumers can purchase at retail are 20 times more concentrated that the fertilizers used in nurseries.

### Jim Foley, 178 Hampstead Road

Mr. Foley stated that a little over a year ago, the applicant came before this Board and said that he was moving to Derry because he wanted to scale back his nursery business; and now he wants to double in size. Mr. Foley stated that the applicant told the Board and abutters that he was going to put up a buffer of arbor vitae trees, and then the applicant went to the ZBA for an oversized commercial backlit sign because the trees block the view of his business.

Mr. Foley stated that the applicant had said that landscaping materials would be delivered by live bottom trucks – while some may be – almost every day the neighborhood hears the banging of hydraulic gates as they deliver materials. Mr. Foley stated that the applicant came to neighbors' houses and promised to be a good neighbor and discussed what he was going to do. Mr. Foley stated that once the applicant obtained approvals, the neighbors have not heard from him since.

Mr. Foley's specific objections include:

1. The plan states that the zoning is LMDR. This is a commercial enterprise stuck in the middle of a residential area. It was a church and was converted, but is still a commercial enterprise, so the setback requirements should still be commercial, not residential.
2. The previous plan cut the number of parking spaces to 110. There is no discussion of parking spaces on the current plan. Northeast Elite Athletics would require 60 parking spaces. Parking spaces are being taken away by adding new storage areas, plant areas, and buildings. How many parking spaces are required per the Town's regulations?

Ms. Robidoux explained the original site plan accounted for the parking requirements. The applicant met the parking need for the two uses on the site. This plan does not change the parking demand. The areas the applicant is using is beyond the parking areas.

Mr. Foley felt the applicant was expanding. Ms. Robidoux stated that there was not proposed expansion into areas where there was existing parking. Mr. Foley felt that strained credibility when part of the discussion before was that no parking of cars would be allowed where equipment was backing up or being used. Ms. Robidoux stated that nothing changed in the upper section of the plan. Mr. Yennaco added that the only change to parking was where the shed was removed, and this gained two parking spaces.

Mr. Foley stated that the Town of Derry's website stated that this area is served by the Pennichuck wells on Olesen Road which pulls water from the aquifer. It is already a stressed aquifer. Mr. Foley is concerned that additional water usage may harm that.

**Site Plan Review -- Redevelopment of Site to Include Restaurant and Bank**

Ms. Robidoux explained the proposal is for the redevelopment of a one story, former bank building with a drive-through. The square footage will remain the same with no additions proposed. Qdoba will add a small outdoor patio in a former green space area. The parking lot has been reconfigured to add spaces on the south side of the parking lot. Spaces were removed to the north side and middle, to accommodate the Exit 4A project and ADA requirements. Fire lanes have been added to the plan and sidewalks will be restored. Parking appears to be adequate for the current uses proposed on site.

The main access point to the site is from Crystal Avenue. The existing condition is being slightly amended to narrow the entrance and exit points to avoid traffic conflicts on Crystal Avenue. The site will be accessed from Crystal via a right in and a right out only. Access to and from the site is also available from the back side of the property adjacent to Citizens Bank.

Mr. Cole was recognized by the Board. This portion of Denali Estates is fairly simple. Phase IV connects the existing Forest Street to the proposed Daniel Road. The Forest Street roadway was a split zoned area; MDR was on the west side and LMDR was on the east side.
